D1_randomisation.why: Sequestered, fixed randomisation schedule (concealed), matching placebo, 1:1.

witnesses.span: Patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous injections of albiglutide or 179 matching placebo once weekly, according to a sequestered, fixed, randomisation schedule.

D2_deviations_assignment.why: All randomised patients analysed whether or not treatment was taken (ITT), matching placebo.

witnesses.span: These analyses included all patients randomly assigned to study 236 treatment, whether taken or not, and followed to the study closure visit (or final date vital 237 status could be ascertained).
Vital status was not known for 61 of 9463 participants (0.6%) (Figure 293 1).

D5_selection_of_reported_result.why: [low on NEW evidence bound after the blind read] The Reporting and Analysis Plan took effect 30-NOV-2017, while close-out visits (from 8 Nov 2017) ran to trial completion in March 2018, and the RAP fixes that planned analyses are performed after database freeze: the plan predates the unblinded data (RoB 2 5.1 = PY). The RAP specifies time to first MACE as the primary analysis.

witnesses.span: Effective Date : 30-NOV-2017 Description : The purpose of this RAP is to describe the planned analyses and output to be included in the Clinical Study Report (CSR) and study disclosure related reporting for Protocol GLP116174.

It is planned that database freeze will occur after the specified number of first MACE events has occurred and that the projected median duration of subject follow-up is at least 1.5 years and subjects complete the final face to face visits. Planned analyses will be performed after database freeze.

Starting 8 November 2017, when it was projected that 611 primary 289 endpoints and a median follow-up of at least 1.5 years had accrued, subjects returned for a final 290 visit and discontinuation from study treatment, with trial completion in March 2018.
Time to first occurrence of MACE (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) The primary analysis will be non-inferiority.
